meta.title: Landscaping in Eastpointe, MI | HD Landscape
meta.description: Beds, sod, grading and hedges for Eastpointe, MI homes on small lots under mature street trees, from HD Landscape next door. Free itemized estimates.

hero.title: Big street trees. Small lots. **Wet ground.**
hero.lede: Almost half of Eastpointe's homes went up in the 1950s, on a street grid lined with mature trees and laid over heavy, slow soil. HD Landscape plans each yard around all three.

about.title: Why a yard here **takes a little planning.**
body: The city's master plan calls the mature trees along most residential streets one of the defining things about its neighborhoods. Bungalows, Cape Cods, ranches and craftsman homes sit on a traditional street grid. The median home dates to 1954, older than in Warren, Roseville or Fraser, so most of these yards have had about seven decades of growth.

Lots are small. Zoning sets the minimum in the low density residential district at 4,000 square feet and 40 feet wide, and the master plan says the smallest lots tend to be toward the center of town. On a lot that size, one overgrown shrub or one low spot is the whole view from the front door.

The ground has always been wet. The city's own history says that by 1835 the Army had laid logs crosswise along what is now Gratiot to lift the road above the water. USDA soil maps agree: every soil they rate in the city is somewhat poorly drained or worse, mostly Lenawee and Toledo silty clay loams. So a low spot in the yard tends to stay wet until the grade changes.

points.title: Mature trees overhead
points.body: Street trees give these blocks their character, and their shade and roots reach well past the sidewalk. We plan grass and beds around the light your yard really gets, so you are not reseeding the same bare patch every spring.

points.title: A city planting more
points.body: The Tree Equity Improvement Program aims to double tree cover from 20 to 40 percent by 2034, with free trees for the strip between your sidewalk and the street. You water them, which is where [plant watering](/plant-watering/) can help.

points.title: Rain and sewage share the pipes
points.body: Macomb County says the 8 1/2 Mile Relief Drain district carries combined stormwater and sanitary flow from all of Eastpointe, and the city ran a rain barrel pilot for that reason. We [grade](/yard-grading/) so water leaves the foundation and heads for the lawn and beds.

points.title: Small lots, fewer plants
points.body: On a 40 foot lot there is no room for a shrub that wants to be 10 feet across. We [choose plants](/landscape-design/) for their full size, keep bed lines simple and leave room to get around the house with a hose.

logistics.title: On lots this close, we plan the way in first.
body: With homes this close together, the first thing to settle is how material gets to the back of the lot and where it can sit. Jake looks at that on site, says what he would tackle first and then writes up an itemized estimate that lays it out line by line.

City yard waste pickup leaves out dirt, sod, large stumps, sand, gravel and rocks, and bags have to stay under 50 pounds. A sod job or a bed tear-out produces exactly that, so none of it can wait at the curb. Your estimate lays out how it gets out of the yard.

faq.q: Do you work in Eastpointe, MI?
faq.a: Yes. HD Landscape works in Eastpointe, which borders St. Clair Shores, where we are based. We take on small lot [landscape design](/landscape-design/) and [renovation](/landscape-renovation/), plus [sod](/sod-installation/), [yard grading](/yard-grading/), [hedge trimming](/hedge-trimming/) and [cleanups](/spring-and-fall-cleanups/). Sprinklers and aeration are outside what we do, and we pass big tree removals to a tree company.

faq.q: Can I get a free tree from the city of Eastpointe?
faq.a: Yes, while funding lasts. The Tree Equity Improvement Program plants free trees in the strip between your sidewalk and the street. You pick from a list of nine species, DPW checks the spot and makes the final call, and you are responsible for watering it. Trees on your side of the walk are not part of the program, and those we can [plant](/plant-installation/) for you.

faq.q: How tall can a hedge be on a corner in Eastpointe?
faq.a: The zoning ordinance limits shrubs, fences and other landscaping to 30 inches inside a clear vision triangle at street corners, measured 25 feet along each right-of-way from the corner. The height is taken from the centerline grade of the street, not from your lawn. Confirm it with the Building Department, since rules change. Our [hedge trimming](/hedge-trimming/) can bring an overgrown corner back down.

faq.q: Why does my yard stay wet after it rains?
faq.a: The soil is the main reason. Most of Eastpointe sits on Lenawee and Toledo silty clay loams, which drain poorly, and the ground is level. [Yard grading](/yard-grading/) can move surface water away from the house. The city has combined sewers, so water coming up through a floor drain is a sewer issue, and no amount of grading will fix it.

faq.q: Will Eastpointe warn me before cutting overgrown grass?
faq.a: Possibly not at your door. The city says its grass notice runs in a newspaper by March 1 and that this is the only notice. Door tags are a courtesy, and the city contractor works independently of them. If you are away, or looking after a family member's house, it pays to keep the yard from getting ahead of you. A [cleanup](/spring-and-fall-cleanups/) can take care of beds and brush.

faq.q: Does Eastpointe pick up sod and dirt from a yard project?
faq.a: No. The city's refuse page says yard waste pickup does not include dirt, sod, large stumps, sand, gravel, concrete or rocks. Leaves, lawn cuttings and shrub trimmings are fine in biodegradable bags under 50 pounds. On a project of ours, how the sod and dirt leave goes on your estimate.
